d: PrismaticConstraint allows two attachments to slide along one axis but not rotate, with optional assigned power for mechanisms like sliding doors and elevator platforms.
h:
For an overview on creating, visualizing, and simulating mechanical constraints, including PrismaticConstraint, see Mechanical constraints. Also see Roblox units to understand how Roblox units compare to metric units.

A PrismaticConstraint creates a rigid joint between two attachments, allowing them to slide along one axis but not rotate. The constraint can also be powered for mechanisms like sliding doors and elevator platforms.

Orientation of a prismatic's attachments affects how it will move. To ensure movement occurs along the desired axis, each attachment's Axis, visualized by the yellow arrow, should point in the same direction.

Linear power

If a prismatic's ActuatorType is set to Motor, it attempts to translate the attachments with the goal of reaching Velocity. You can further control this translation through both MotorMaxAcceleration and MotorMaxForce.

If a prismatic's ActuatorType is set to Servo, it attempts to translate the attachments to a set separation specified by TargetPosition. This translation is controlled by Speed, LinearResponsiveness, and ServoMaxForce.

Limits

You can set limits to restrict the sliding range a prismatic. Enabling the LimitsEnabled property exposes the LowerLimit and UpperLimit values, as well as Restitution which defines the elasticity of the attachments when they reach either limit.

kid.simple: A PrismaticConstraint lets two parts slide along one straight line but never rotate. Think sliding doors, elevators, drawers and pistons. You can power it as a motor that keeps sliding at a speed, or as a servo that moves to an exact distance and stops. Limits keep it from sliding too far.
kid.analogy: It is like a drawer on its rails: it slides in and out along one line, but it cannot twist or tip over.
keyPoints: A prismatic constraint allows sliding along one axis only, with no rotation.
The sliding direction is the attachments' yellow Axis arrow. Make both attachments point the same way.
`ActuatorType = Motor` slides toward a speed set by `Velocity`, limited by `MotorMaxForce` and `MotorMaxAcceleration`.
`ActuatorType = Servo` slides to a distance set by `TargetPosition`, using `Speed`, `LinearResponsiveness` and `ServoMaxForce`.
Turn on `LimitsEnabled` to set `LowerLimit` and `UpperLimit`, so it cannot slide past them.
`Restitution` controls how bouncy it is when it hits a limit.

terms.attachment: A Roblox object you put inside a part to mark one exact point on it. Its Position is measured from the part's center, so an attachment at (-2, 0, 0) sits 2 studs toward the part's own left side.
terms.Axis: Every attachment has its own arrows. `Axis` (yellow arrow) is its main X direction and `SecondaryAxis` (orange arrow) is its Y direction. With Orientation (0, 0, 0) the yellow arrow points along the part's X; with Orientation (0, 0, 90) it is turned a quarter turn to point straight up.
terms.translate: Move in a straight line without turning.
terms.TargetPosition: How far apart, in studs along the axis, the servo tries to move the two attachments. 20 means 20 studs apart.
terms.Velocity / Speed: Studs per second. A servo `Speed` of 5 covers 20 studs in 4 seconds.
terms.ServoMaxForce: The strongest push the servo can make. It must beat gravity: an 8 x 1 x 8 Plastic platform has mass 64 x 0.7 = 44.8, so it weighs about 44.8 x 196.2 = 8790 force units, before any riders.
terms.LinearResponsiveness: How sharply the servo reacts. Higher means snappier movement.
terms.limits: The lowest and highest allowed positions, in studs.
terms.restitution: How bouncy the stop is when a moving piece hits its limit. 0 means it stops dead, 1 means it bounces back as hard as it hit.

example.title: An elevator platform that goes up and down
example.code:
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local base = Instance.new("Part")
base.Size = Vector3.new(8, 1, 8)
base.Position = Vector3.new(0, 0.5, 30)
base.Anchored = true
base.Parent = Workspace

local platform = Instance.new("Part")
platform.Size = Vector3.new(8, 1, 8)   -- mass = 64 * 0.7 = 44.8
platform.Position = Vector3.new(0, 1.5, 30)
platform.BrickColor = BrickColor.new("Bright green")
platform.Parent = Workspace

-- Orientation (0, 0, 90) makes each attachment's X axis point straight up,
-- so the platform slides vertically
local baseAtt = Instance.new("Attachment")
baseAtt.Orientation = Vector3.new(0, 0, 90)
baseAtt.Parent = base

local platformAtt = Instance.new("Attachment")
platformAtt.Orientation = Vector3.new(0, 0, 90)
platformAtt.Parent = platform

local slider = Instance.new("PrismaticConstraint")
slider.Attachment0 = baseAtt
slider.Attachment1 = platformAtt
slider.ActuatorType = Enum.ActuatorType.Servo
slider.Speed = 5               -- studs per second
slider.ServoMaxForce = 100000  -- much more than the platform's weight (about 8790)
slider.LimitsEnabled = true
slider.LowerLimit = 0
slider.UpperLimit = 20
slider.Parent = base

while true do
	slider.TargetPosition = 20  -- go up: 20 studs at 5 studs per second = 4 seconds
	task.wait(6)
	slider.TargetPosition = 1   -- come back down
	task.wait(6)
end
explain: The base is anchored. The platform starts right on top of it, with its center 1 stud above the base's center.
Both attachments use Orientation (0, 0, 90), turning their yellow arrow to point up, so the slide line is vertical.
`TargetPosition` is the distance between the two attachments along that line. Going from 1 to 20 is 19 studs, which takes about 3.8 seconds at `Speed = 5`.
`ServoMaxForce` must beat gravity. The platform weighs about 44.8 x 196.2 = 8790, and players riding it add more, so 100000 gives plenty of extra.
Limits from 0 to 20 stop the platform from ever sliding outside that range.

watchOut: If the platform slides sideways instead of up, the attachments' Axis arrows point the wrong way. Turn on Show Constraint Details to check.
If the elevator sags or will not lift players, `ServoMaxForce` is too low. Remember to count the weight of the platform plus riders.
`TargetPosition` is a distance between attachments, not a world height. If the attachments start 1 stud apart, the position starts at 1.
